title: Canyon Run
description: Canyon Run is a React Native app that helps runners track and visualize their routes using GPS.
overview: A mobile running companion with interactive route visualization, altitude stats, and auto-saving so the user never loses a run in progress.
demoTitle: Route tracking that stays visible while you run
demoDescription: The app centers the map, route path, and stats so runners can see distance, elevation, and progress without digging through menus.

diagramSteps.title: Capture
diagramSteps.detail: GPS points are collected while the runner is moving.

diagramSteps.title: Visualize
diagramSteps.detail: The route is drawn on the map with supporting altitude stats.

diagramSteps.title: Persist
diagramSteps.detail: Sessions are auto-saved so the user can review them later.

systemDesign: The app is organized around a lightweight session model: capture location updates, render the path in real time, and persist the completed route for later review. That keeps the UI responsive while still making the run data durable.
learned: I learned how important state recovery is in mobile apps, especially when GPS data and autosave need to feel seamless to the user.

title: Insert
description: Recipe app built with React Native, MongoDB, and AWS.
overview: A cross-platform recipe experience with cloud-backed data storage and a mobile-first interface for browsing and saving meals.
demoDescription: The layout is designed around quick browsing, recipe previews, and straightforward save actions so users can move fast in the kitchen.

diagramSteps.title: Request
diagramSteps.detail: The mobile app requests recipe data from the backend.

diagramSteps.title: Store
diagramSteps.detail: MongoDB keeps the recipe content and user data organized.

diagramSteps.title: Deliver
diagramSteps.detail: AWS hosts the app and makes the experience accessible across devices.

systemDesign: The system separates the mobile UI from the persistent data layer, which keeps the app easier to scale and simpler to maintain. MongoDB provides flexible content storage while AWS handles deployment and availability.
learned: I learned how to combine mobile UX with a cloud-backed architecture so the product can grow beyond a local prototype.

title: ESP32-Tamogatchi-Clone
description: ESP32-based Tamagotchi clone featuring SSD1306 OLED display, three GPIO buttons, and active buzzer interaction.
overview: A playful embedded project that combines hardware buttons, display output, and sound feedback to recreate the classic virtual pet experience.
demoTitle: A tiny pet with real hardware feedback
demoDescription: The display, buttons, and buzzer work together to give the user visible and audible feedback as the virtual pet changes state.

diagramSteps.title: Input
diagramSteps.detail: GPIO buttons capture the player’s actions.

diagramSteps.title: Process
diagramSteps.detail: The ESP32 updates the pet’s state and logic.

diagramSteps.title: Output
diagramSteps.detail: The OLED and buzzer provide visible and audible feedback.

systemDesign: The project uses a simple embedded event loop: capture button input, update the virtual pet state, and reflect that state on the OLED with sound cues. That keeps the logic predictable and easy to debug on hardware.
learned: I learned how hardware constraints shape software design, especially when you need fast, understandable feedback from a very small interface.
